pharm: Nelfinavir mesylate selectively binds the active site of the HIV-1 protease enzyme, preventing cleavage of the gag-pol polyprotein and producing immature, non-infectious virions. It is a substrate of CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 and a moderate inhibitor of CYP3A4, the basis for its extensive drug interactions. Oral absorption is markedly increased by food, so it must be taken with a meal.

Not preferred; hepatic events reported - consider alternative PIs

summary: Nelfinavir (Viracept) is an oral HIV-1 protease inhibitor used in combination with other antiretroviral agents to treat HIV-1 infection. It blocks the viral protease that matures new virions, halting production of infectious virus. Because it must be taken with food for adequate absorption and is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and CYP2C19/3A4 substrate, it has extensive and clinically important drug interactions, including absolute contraindications with potent CYP3A4-dependent drugs (certain statins, ergots, oral midazolam/triazolam, pimozide, amiodarone, quinidine, rifampin, St. John's wort). Diarrhea is the most common adverse effect. It should not be used in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults, adolescents, and children, in combination with other antiretroviral agents

dosage.t: Twice or three times daily with a meal
dosage.n: Always administer with food to optimize absorption

dosage.c: HIV-1 infection (children 2 to <13 yr) - twice-daily option
dosage.n: Weight-band tablet/powder tables provided in labeling

admin: Take with a meal every time - food increases nelfinavir exposure 2-5 fold and is required for efficacy
Use only in combination with other antiretroviral agents, never as monotherapy
Tablets may be dispersed in a small amount of water if needed; the oral powder may be mixed with water, milk, or formula (not acidic foods/juice and use within 6 hours)
Separate didanosine: give didanosine 1 hour before or 2 or more hours after nelfinavir
Avoid acid-suppressing proton pump inhibitors, which lower nelfinavir levels
Review the full medication list for CYP3A4 interactions before starting
moa: Nelfinavir is a selective, competitive inhibitor of the HIV-1 protease, an aspartyl protease essential for processing the viral gag and gag-pol polyprotein precursors. By binding the protease active site, nelfinavir prevents cleavage of these precursors into the mature structural and enzymatic proteins required for virion maturation, resulting in production of immature, non-infectious viral particles. It does not require intracellular phosphorylation and is active against HIV-1 in acutely and chronically infected cells. Pharmacologically it is metabolized by CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 and inhibits CYP3A4, accounting for its drug-interaction profile.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to nelfinavir or any component
Concomitant drugs highly dependent on CYP3A4 with narrow therapeutic windows: lovastatin, simvastatin (myopathy/rhabdomyolysis)
Ergot derivatives - dihydroergotamine, ergotamine, methylergonovine (ergot toxicity)
Oral midazolam and triazolam (prolonged/excessive sedation, respiratory depression)
Rifampin (markedly reduces nelfinavir concentrations - loss of efficacy/resistance)
St. John's wort (reduces nelfinavir levels - loss of efficacy/resistance)
relative: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment (avoid use)
monitor: Severity of diarrhea and GI tolerability

preg: Antiretroviral therapy is recommended in pregnancy, but nelfinavir is not a preferred agent. Reports of hepatic adverse events ranging from elevated liver enzymes to hepatic failure have occurred in pregnant patients exposed to nelfinavir. Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry data show a first-trimester birth-defect rate of about 3.9% versus a 2.7% background rate. Consider alternative, preferred antiretroviral drugs during pregnancy.
lact: In the United States, mothers with HIV-1 are instructed NOT to breastfeed because of the risk of postnatal HIV transmission. It is not known whether nelfinavir is excreted in human milk. The decision reflects HIV transmission risk rather than direct drug toxicity.
renal: The pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy of nelfinavir have not been established in patients with renal impairment. Because nelfinavir is highly protein bound and primarily eliminated via feces with minimal urinary excretion, significant renal accumulation is not expected, but use with caution as data are lacking.
hepatic: Nelfinavir should NOT be used in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment, in whom exposure is increased. No dose adjustment is required for mild hepatic impairment, but monitor liver function. Discontinue if signs of clinically significant hepatotoxicity occur.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, St. John's wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) - lower nelfinavir levels, risk of resistance
CYP3A4 substrates with narrow index (see contraindications) - life-threatening toxicity
Atorvastatin - limit to maximum 40 mg/day; consider pravastatin/fluvastatin instead
PDE5 inhibitors - max sildenafil 25 mg/48 h, vardenafil 2.5 mg/24 h, tadalafil 10 mg/72 h
Hormonal contraceptives - decreased ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone; use an additional or alternative non-hormonal method
Proton pump inhibitors - decrease nelfinavir exposure; avoid coadministration
moderate: Rifabutin - increases rifabutin exposure (halve rifabutin dose) and decreases nelfinavir (use 1250 mg BID)
Anticonvulsants metabolized by/affecting CYP - monitor levels and antiviral response
Methadone - nelfinavir may decrease methadone levels
minor: Didanosine - administer 1 hour before or 2 or more hours after nelfinavir to avoid the food/acid effect
interactions.food: Nelfinavir MUST be taken with a meal; food increases absorption 2-5 fold and is required for therapeutic exposure.
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacokinetic interaction with alcohol is described; limit alcohol given the potential for additive hepatic injury.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause elevated liver enzymes, hyperglycemia, and dyslipidemia; oral powder contains phenylalanine (relevant in PKU).

rare: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes (postmarketing)
emergency: Torsades de pointes or serious arrhythmia

monitoring: Severity and persistence of diarrhea (most common adverse effect)
Liver function tests, especially in pregnancy and with hepatic risk factors
Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count for antiviral response
counsel: Always take this medicine WITH a meal - it will not work properly on an empty stomach
Take it exactly on schedule along with your other HIV medicines; do not skip doses
Diarrhea is the most common side effect - report severe or persistent diarrhea and stay hydrated
Tell every prescriber and pharmacist you take nelfinavir - it has many serious drug interactions
Do not start any new prescription, over-the-counter drug, or herbal product (especially St. John's wort) without checking
Use an additional or non-hormonal birth-control method, as this drug can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives
This medicine controls HIV but does not cure it and does not prevent passing HIV to others
pk: Antiviral effect over days-weeks; steady state in ~2-3 days
Plasma Tmax ~2-3 hours after a dose taken with food
Dosed two or three times daily with meals
Store at 15-30 C (59-86 F) in a tightly closed container
pearls: Must be taken WITH food - food increases exposure 2-5 fold and is essential for efficacy
Diarrhea is the most common adverse effect and a frequent reason for discontinuation
Potent CYP3A4 interactions - absolutely avoid lovastatin/simvastatin, ergots, oral midazolam/triazolam, pimozide, amiodarone, quinidine, rifampin, and St. John's wort
Decreases hormonal contraceptive levels - advise an additional/alternative method
Do not use in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment; watch for hepatotoxicity, especially in pregnancy
Separate didanosine and avoid proton pump inhibitors, which lower nelfinavir levels
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember with a snack or meal. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule with food. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for nelfinavir overdose. If indicated, eliminate unabsorbed drug by emesis or gastric lavage and consider activated charcoal. Because nelfinavir is highly protein bound (>98%), dialysis is unlikely to remove significant drug. Management is supportive, with monitoring of vital signs and clinical status.
